items.title: A Model For Everyone: How Ronak From Trajectory Is Building Products For Continual Learning
items.text: Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:32 A lot of our philosophy in product actually comes from Apple. In, like, the early two thousands, you had a computer that had access to the Internet, and you had a phone that you could make phone calls. And I think no one really thought to put the two together until Apple said, okay. What if you actually put the Internet on a handheld device and combine the two? And I think by doing this of of basically putting training, eval, and deployment in one place, making that just dead simple for every single person to do, And then you can close the loop and basically now upload that model back to production, gather new traces. There’s no substitute to really using the models for your workflows to understand the best ones that actually work for your workflows. In reality, there’s only very very few benchmarks that truly matter, and the real ones know. Rest is primarily posturing or hill climbing on one just to use as marketing (which in reality does work for a select group of companies but won’t last over time)
